# MCMCResult { #deep_tensor.MCMCResult }

```python
MCMCResult(self, chain: MarkovChain)
```

An object containing a constructed Markov chain.

## Attributes {.doc-section .doc-section-attributes}

<code>[**xs**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [Tensor]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   An $n \times k$ matrix containing the samples that form the  Markov chain.

<code>[**potentials**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [Tensor]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   An $n$-dimensional vector containing the potential function  associated with the target density evaluated at each sample in  the chain.

<code>[**acceptance_rate**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   The acceptance rate of the sampler.

<code>[**iacts**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [Tensor]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   A $k$-dimensional vector containing estimates of the integrated  autocorrelation time (IACT) for each parameter.

<code>[**ess**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [Tensor]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   A $k$-dimensional vector containing estimates of the effective  sample size (ESS) of each parameter.

## Notes {.doc-section .doc-section-notes}

The IACT for parameter $i$, denoted using $\tau_{i}$, is estimated 
using the monotone sequence estimator outlined by Geyer (2011).

## References {.doc-section .doc-section-references}

Geyer, CJ (2011). *[Introduction to Markov chain Monte Carlo](https://doi.org/10.1201/b10905)*. 
In: Handbook of Markov Chain Monte Carlo 3--48.
